title: The Star: Q1 FY27 EBITDA A$12m vs A$13m Loss
caption:
The Announcement Room | The Star Entertainment Group Limited (SGR)

The Star Entertainment Group reported Q1 FY27 Group EBITDA of A$12 million for the quarter to 30 September 2026, against a A$13 million loss in the same quarter last year. Sydney and Gold Coast revenue rose 5% to A$279 million, the first year-on-year increase since the company began quarterly reporting.

Costs did much of the work. Group operating expenses fell 12% to A$202 million and unallocated corporate costs fell 29% to A$23 million. Cash flow was weaker: net operating cash flow was -A$15.5 million, cash and equivalents fell to A$239 million from A$267 million, and the company says going-concern uncertainties from FY26 remain.

Key points:

• Group EBITDA was A$12 million, up A$25 million on the prior year
• Sydney and Gold Coast revenue was A$279 million, up 5% on the prior year and 9% on Q4 FY26
• Sydney property EBITDA rose to A$15 million from A$3 million
• Gold Coast property EBITDA rose to A$20 million from A$11 million
• Brisbane operator fee fell to A$5 million from A$14 million under the amended management agreement
• Net operating cash flow was -A$15.5 million, including one-off items the filing does not quantify
• The Sydney casino licence remains suspended

Looking ahead, management expects FY27 to be the first year in more than two years with net operating cash inflows before one-off items. That is an expectation, not a result. The company will reassess its going-concern position when it files half-year accounts, and says it cannot assure investors the uncertainties will be resolved by then.

In this two-page investor report, we look at:

• Where the EBITDA improvement came from
• Why the Q1 FY27 result is not the first positive quarter
• What the cash flow and cash balance show
• Licence status and what to watch next
